column1: The project SDK recommended for new SQL database projects is {{c1::Microsoft.Build.Sql}}.
column2:
Original SQL projects instead use the older MSBuild format based on .NET Framework.
Review source

column1: A SQL project's build produces a {{c1::.dacpac}} artifact containing the compiled database schema model.
column2:
The normal project build packages schema rather than a backup of the database's table data.
Review source

column1: SDK-style SQL projects include .sql files in the project folder tree through {{c1::default globbing}}.
column2:
Globbing selects files by a filename pattern, so individual model files need no explicit Build Include entry.
Review source

column1: Install the command-line SQL project templates with {{c1::dotnet new install Microsoft.Build.Sql.Templates}}.
column2:
Install a supported .NET SDK before using the dotnet commands.
Review source

column1: With the SQL templates installed, create MyDatabaseProject using {{c1::dotnet new sqlproj -n MyDatabaseProject}}.
column2:
The command creates a new SDK-style SQL project.
Review source

column1: Build the SDK-style project MyDatabaseProject.sqlproj with {{c1::dotnet build MyDatabaseProject.sqlproj}}.
column2:
The build validates the model and produces a deployable artifact without publishing it.
Review source

column1: A default Debug build places a SQL project's .dacpac in {{c1::bin\Debug}}.
column2:
Custom output paths and other build configurations can change this location.
Review source

column1: A SQL project's target platform is stored in the {{c1::DSP}} property.
column2:
For example, Microsoft.Data.Tools.Schema.Sql.Sql170DatabaseSchemaProvider targets SQL Server 2025.
Review source

column1: Install SqlPackage as a global .NET tool with {{c1::dotnet tool install --global microsoft.sqlpackage}}.
column2:
The .NET tool runs on Windows, Linux, and macOS with a supported runtime.
Review source

column1: SqlPackage applies a .dacpac to a database with {{c1::/Action:Publish}}.
column2:
Supply /SourceFile for the artifact and /TargetConnectionString for the destination connection.
Review source

column1: Enable SQL code analysis during a project build with {{c1::RunSqlCodeAnalysis}} set to True.
column2:
Configure SqlCodeAnalysisRules to select rules and their warning or error behavior.
Review source

column1: SQL project configuration, including its target platform, resides in the {{c1::.sqlproj}} file.
column2:
Database object definitions normally reside in separate .sql files.
